title: More Than Just Access: Generative AI as Communication Intermediary for Blind and Low-Vision Users
abstract: arXiv:2609.15696v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) tools are increasingly woven into how blind and low-vision (BLV) people communicate, not only with digital information, but with the physical world and with other people. Tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Be My AI, and Seeing AI translate visual and textual content into accessible form, and are beginning to substitute for interpersonal requests for help, such as asking a family member to read a label or describe a scene. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 19 BLV participants, we examine GenAI as a communication intermediary and how it succeeds and fails as an alternative for reading, describing, and even asking another person for help. We also investigated what BLV users gain and risk when these tools take over that role. translated_title: 超越无障碍访问：生成式AI作为盲人与低视力用户的沟通中介
translated_abstract: 生成式人工智能（GenAI）工具正日益融入盲人与低视力（BLV）人群的沟通方式，不仅涉及数字信息，还涉及与物理世界及他人的交流。ChatGPT、Google Gemini、Be My AI 和 Seeing AI 等工具能够将视觉和文本内容转化为无障碍形式，并开始取代人际求助，例如请家人阅读标签或描述场景。通过对19名BLV参与者进行半结构化访谈，我们考察了GenAI作为沟通中介的角色，以及它在替代阅读、描述、甚至向他人求助等方面的成功与失败。我们还研究了当这些工具承担这一角色时，BLV用户的收益与风险。最后，我们提出了针对GenAI系统的设计与政策启示：系统应诚实地传达不确定性、保护用户信息，并支持BLV用户的独立性而非取代他们。
tldr: 本研究通过对19名盲人与低视力用户的访谈，揭示了生成式AI作为沟通中介在替代人际帮助时的作用与局限，指出用户既获得了独立性也面临隐私风险，并提出GenAI系统应诚实传达不确定性、保护信息并支持用户独立性的设计与政策建议。
en_tdlr: Through interviews with 19 blind and low-vision participants, this study examines generative AI as a communication intermediary that substitutes for interpersonal help, revealing the independence users gain, the risks they face, and proposing design and policy implications for GenAI systems to communicate uncertainty honestly, protect information, and support user independence.
